snippetsFromFirstPass./bridging-loans-uk/: provides bridging loans UK wide, with a strong focus on the London property market; aimed at homeowners, investors and developers; uses: buying before selling a current home, funding a renovation, covering a short-term cash flow gap; loans typically set up for 12 to 24 months and secured on property; interest is rolled up rather than paid monthly, so no affordability check is needed; principal and interest repaid as one sum on expiry, usually via refinancing or sale; cites 700+ Lenders.
snippetsFromFirstPass./commercial-mortgage-broker/: London-based commercial mortgage broker specializing in large loans of £2-£20m; 'the firm also focuses on larger loan sizes of £2-£20 million which sets us apart from the majority of the commercial bridging loan market'; typically narrows lenders to as many as 3 or 4 potential partners.
snippetsFromFirstPass./property-development-finance/: flexible property development finance for residential, commercial, or mixed-use projects; loans fund real estate schemes (either ground-up or conversions) of any nature; secured against the available land and drawn in line with the business plan and construction schedule; interest rolled up; repaid at practical completion through sales or refinance; access to a vast network of senior debt, mezzanine debt and equity lenders; 300+ lenders; as many as 3 or 4 potential partners per deal.
snippetsFromFirstPass./types-of-borrowing/: older overview: 'We can help with your wealth management.' Sections: development finance (senior, stretched senior, mezzanine/second charge, joint venture equity; broker fees around 1%; worked example at 6.5% fixed), bridging finance ('quick to arrange and do not require any affordability assessment'; interest paid as lump sum at end), prime residential mortgages (£5m and above; policies vary by private bank branch); retail outlets as income-producing asset class; each lender has its own appetite for property types.
snippetsFromFirstPass./faq/: HMO max LTV typically 75%, some lenders 80% in exceptional circumstances; Article 4 direction can help valuations; BTL products max out at 75% LTV (25% deposit); Consumer Buy-to-Let can fall under FCA rules; 'If you or a family member occupies more than 40% of the property, it becomes a regulated loan'; non-resident lending needs stronger documentation, more conservative LTV, path of funds (AML/KYC); 'A portfolio loan can sit alongside existing individual mortgages'; premium on portfolio products has narrowed; whole-loan providers often sector-agnostic: PBSA, hotels, BTR, industrial; some lenders allow first-time HMO buyers with strong personal income and clear management plan; network of over 800 lenders.
snippetsFromFirstPass./introducers/: can arrange commercial mortgages, buy-to-let mortgages, bridging loans, development finance, marine finance, or aviation finance; pays 'a competitive percentage of our procurement fee upon the successful completion of the loan', details agreed upfront; once indicative terms are provided, introducers introduce the borrower directly.
snippetsFromFirstPass./lenders/: generally focuses on transactions upwards of £500,000; works with an unrestricted number of lenders and typically receives commission from lenders, with details disclosed during the process.
snippetsFromFirstPass./lender-calculator/: tool estimating borrowing capacity, loan terms and repayments for commercial and development finance across the UK; select project type, loan type, loan size and term; shows how many lenders are willing to lend on a particular project.
snippetsFromFirstPass./western-europe/: regularly act for clients from Africa, Asia and the Middle East who are purchasing properties in Europe and the UK; popular with investors from countries with volatile currencies, such as South Africa or Turkey; frequently arranges facilities for offshore trusts and overseas owners.
snippetsFromFirstPass./about-us/: Jimmy Baillie, Managing Director, founded the firm in 2019; 'has focused on loans between £500K to £20m'; 'Types Of Properties' list (student accommodation confirmed); 'one of Europe's leading large loan brokers'; Spear's profile: run from London and South Africa; advises UHNW clients on secured loans £2m–£20m; deals in UK, Western Europe, Southern Africa, Middle East; clients from UK, France, Spain, Dubai, South Africa.
snippetsFromFirstPass./contact/: three routes: enquiry form, direct email, WhatsApp; office 91 Wimpole Street, London W1G 0EE.
snippetsFromFirstPass./how-does-property-development-finance-i: types: senior loans, mezzanine finance, bridging loans, stretched senior loans, joint venture finance; 'Senior development loans cover a percentage of land purchase and construction costs, typically up to 65-75% of Gross Development Value.'; mezzanine 'a secondary loan that sits behind senior debt, reducing the developer's equity requirement'.
snippetsFromFirstPass./how-does-property-development-finance-w: 'One of the most common ways in which development finance is structured is a series of tranches.' Sequence: buy land/existing property, obtain planning approval, fund in tranches.
snippetsFromFirstPass./development-finance-ltv-ltc-and-ltgdv-e: LTV = loan / current value; LTC = loan / total development cost; LTGDV = loan / gross development value.
